title: Events in courses: ideas from other products
intro: This page gathers ideas for the Events step inside Courses in Essentials 2.0. It shows how instructors create and edit scheduled events inside a course, such as simulation sessions, live classes, labs and exam slots. It covers date and time, room and equipment, which scenarios run, which learner groups attend, facilitators, capacity and recurrence. The calendar overview and telling learners about dates sit in sub-module 10; scenarios (05) and learner groups (04) are neighbouring topics. Examples come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero.

questions.title: Where do instructors create events: inside the course, or on a global calendar tagged to the course?
questions.answer: Two places to create events show up, and Kajabi has both in one product. Kajabi schedules sessions inside a coaching product, and it also has a separate Marketing, then Events calendar with no product link. Luma is the global calendar with a tag: the create form starts with 'Create under [calendar]', so you pick the container when you create the event. Acuity defines a reusable class type first, then offers an instance on a date. Calendly and TravelPerk are global-only lists with one Create button. Circle is the cautionary case. It has course spaces, yet its create-event form sits under the global Events tab. Its 'scheduled' course space flow drips lessons rather than bookable sessions. For an instructor building a course calendar, creating inside the course wins because the course is already the context. The global calendar should be a filtered view with the course as a tag. No example shows a course page listing events that were created on a global calendar. That is the gap module 10 has to close.

questions.title: How do products link content and groups to the event, and can you see that link both ways?
questions.answer: Only Understory shows an explicit step from content to event. '+ Event' opens 'Select the experience', and the form then arrives pre-filled with capacity, location, resources, rooms and guides. Workable gets the same effect by opening the event from the record, so the title and context are already filled in. HubSpot is the one product that treats the group as an object. The event side panel has 'Associated campaign' and 'Lists' sections, though both are empty in the screenshot. Luma and Rise link the event to individual attendees with statuses, not to a cohort. Nothing in the set shows the other direction, such as a scenario or group page listing its sessions, and nothing attaches a learner group as a unit. Preply is the example of what not to copy here: a one-to-one lesson with nothing to link. For Essentials the event form should start from the scenario, as Understory does, and accept learner groups as objects, as HubSpot lists do. Both the scenario and the group should list their sessions. That reverse link has to be designed without an example.

questions.title: How do products handle recurrence and editing a series (this, following, or all)?
questions.answer: A repeat rule at creation is common. Zoom, Understory and Amie show frequency, weekdays and an end condition. Skiff also shows a customise pop-up and the instances on the calendar. Edit scope is thinner than expected: Amie and Motion both ask 'this event' or 'all events', and no example in this set offers the three-way 'this and following'. Luma is the only product that builds a series from an existing single event. You choose 'Create multi-session event', add recurring sessions or a manual session list, and the event shows '+9 sessions'. Acuity is the example of what not to copy here: rescheduling one class instance shows a plain date and time panel with no scope question. Simulation sessions rarely repeat identically because groups rotate through scenarios, so Luma's explicit session list fits better than a bare repeat rule. The two-option scope dialog is still needed when a whole series moves.

questions.title: How do products show room, facilitator or equipment conflicts when creating an event?
questions.answer: Every conflict message found is a soft warning after the fact, never a block inside the creation form. Acuity reopens a class with a yellow banner naming the resource ('uses resource Room #5') and still saves. Fresha warns that the staff member is not working at that time, with Apply still enabled. Clockwise says 'I can schedule this meeting, but there is a conflict for Sam'. 7shifts batches the check at publish time, counting conflicts and offering 'fix them for me'. Google Workspace has a room and equipment picker with capacity but no availability feedback. SavvyCal's 'Ignore calendar conflicts' switch implies detection exists elsewhere. Zoom only complains at join time. Understory models resources with quantities, yet its session pop-up shows no conflict feedback at all, which is the example of what not to copy. No product shows equipment-specific conflicts. For a simulation centre, rooms, manikins and facilitators are the scarce resources. The pattern to adopt is warn and do not block, but moved into the form as live availability per resource. No example shows that.

questions.title: How do products handle capacity, sign-up and attendance?
questions.answer: Three sign-up models appear. Self sign-up: Aboard's single 'Attend' switch, and Partiful's RSVP with a plus-one, where spots drop per person from 20/20 to 18/20. Approval required: Luma's guest list moves people from Pending approval to Going under a cap of 1,000. Host-added: SavvyCal lets the organiser invite a guest after scheduling. Capacity is a number field with a 'no limit' option in Understory, and per ticket tier plus an event total in Eventbrite. Attendance is always marked by the host. Posh switches a guest to Checked in. Lyssna offers Mark as completed or No-show and marks sessions complete automatically after five days. No example shows a waitlist or attendee self check-in. In Essentials attendance is mostly assigned through the learner group. The useful borrowings are the capacity field with a no-limit option, Posh's check-in and Lyssna's automatic resolution of unmarked sessions.

questions.title: How do products handle time zone and duration?
questions.answer: An explicit time-zone selector is the norm. Microsoft Teams leads the form with the zone, then start and end with a computed duration and an all-day switch. Cal.com shows the zone on both the availability page and the booking page. Kajabi, SavvyCal and Clockwise pair the zone with duration presets and an availability grid. Zoom is the exception on duration, taking free hours and minutes. Homerun uses start plus a duration dropdown and shows the zone only as a read-only label. That is the example of what not to copy for the explicit selector. Upwork is the only product that previews the other party's local time ('2:16 PM GMT+8, 2h ahead'). Simulation sessions happen in a physical centre, so one institutional zone shown as a label is enough. Duration should default from the scenario's running time in module 05, which makes Homerun's start-plus-duration model the closest fit.

references.title: Define class type, then schedule instance
references.question: Q1
references.take: Acuity separates defining the reusable class or appointment type in a global catalog from scheduling an instance on the calendar.

references.title: Global events list with Create
references.question: Q1
references.take: Calendly lists all scheduled events in one global dashboard with a single Create action. Creation does not live inside a course or project.

references.title: Create event under global Events tab
references.question: Q1
references.take: Circle's create-event form opens under the global Events tab, not inside a course space. It has date and time, a repeat rule and an end date, with no course field.

references.title: Scheduled course setup with dates and groups
references.question: Q1
references.take: Circle's full scheduled course creation shows date and group selection inside course setup. It shows scheduling next to group context inside the course.

references.title: Course sessions list with reschedule
references.question: Q1
references.take: Kajabi lists sessions inside the course detail view, each with a reschedule action.

references.title: Event form with time zone and repeat
references.question: Q1
references.take: Kajabi's event form has a title, date and time, time zone and a recurrence interval selector.

references.title: Schedule coaching session from course
references.question: Q1
references.take: Kajabi's session scheduling flow starts from the course coaching context. It covers the calendar, availability setup and time-slot selection.

references.title: Create event and pick owning calendar
references.question: Q1
references.take: Luma requires choosing or creating a 'calendar' as the container when you create an event. That is a global calendar with a tag, not creation inside a course.

references.title: My lessons list with 'Schedule lesson'
references.question: Q1
references.take: Preply schedules lessons inside the instructor context. The 'Schedule lesson' button creates events there.

references.title: Create team event from global Events
references.question: Q1
references.take: TravelPerk creates events from a dedicated global Events area, then shows a detail overview. That sits apart from any project or course.

references.title: Event details with campaign and lists
references.question: Q2
references.take: HubSpot's event panel shows attendees, an associated campaign link and lists. It shows rich links around the event.

references.title: Invite stats with acceptance status
references.question: Q2
references.take: Luma's invite stats panel shows all attendees with acceptance status. The event and the people link both ways.

references.title: Reschedule lesson from student list
references.question: Q2
references.take: Preply reschedules a one-to-one lesson from the list to a menu to a new slot. There is no content selection and no group.

references.title: Event details with participant list
references.question: Q2
references.take: Rise's event details panel shows participant avatars and names. People are linked from inside the event.

references.title: Pick Experience before adding resources
references.question: Q2
references.take: Understory's event creation requires selecting an existing Experience before you add capacity and resources. Content is linked to the event in an explicit step.

references.title: Interview with linked candidate and role
references.question: Q2
references.take: Workable's interview event shows the linked candidate and role. The candidate has the event, and the event has the candidate.

references.title: Reschedule one class on weekly calendar
references.question: Q3
references.take: Acuity reschedules one class instance with a plain date and time panel. It does not ask whether to change this event or all events.

references.title: Repeat dialog with days and end date
references.question: Q3
references.take: Amie's Repeat pop-up lets you set frequency, such as every 2 weeks, pick days with checkboxes, and choose an end date.

references.title: Update series: this event or all events
references.question: Q3
references.take: When you edit a recurring event, Amie asks you to choose between 'This event' and 'All events' radio buttons.

references.title: Turn one event into multi-session series
references.question: Q3
references.take: Luma turns a single event into a multi-session series. A pop-up lets you add sessions by hand or set a recurring cadence.

references.title: Update series: this event or all events
references.question: Q3
references.take: Motion shows 'This event' and 'All events' options as radio buttons when you update a recurring series.

references.title: Customise recurring event on calendar
references.question: Q3
references.take: Skiff turns Repeats on, sets frequency, then opens 'Customize recurring event' for every, on and ends. Instances appear on the calendar. No edit-scope dialog appears in these screenshots.

references.title: Custom recurrence rule with end date
references.question: Q3
references.take: Understory puts custom recurrence in its own dialog with an explicit end-date picker. The end condition is set apart from the base date and location.

references.title: Recurring meeting frequency and weekdays
references.question: Q3
references.take: Zoom's recurring meeting setup shows repeat frequency such as Weekly, weekday checkboxes from Sun to Sat, and an end date with an occurrence count option.

references.title: Publish warnings for shift conflicts
references.question: Q4
references.take: 7shifts shows a warning dialog with exception counts before publishing schedule changes, including Exceptions, Conflicts, Overtime warning and Unassigned Shifts.

references.title: Conflict warning naming blocked room
references.question: Q4
references.take: Acuity's event detail panel shows an explicit conflict warning that names the blocked room and time when you open a class that overlaps another booking.

references.title: Person conflict warnings on calendar
references.question: Q4
references.take: Clockwise shows conflict alerts on the calendar, including 'I can schedule this meeting, but there is a conflict' and 'Sam has conflicts that I can't fix'.

references.title: Staff not working during booking slot
references.question: Q4
references.take: Fresha warns that 'Alex Smith is not working between 7:00am and 7:45am' when the staff member is unavailable for the booking slot.

references.title: Room and equipment picker with capacity
references.question: Q4
references.take: Google Workspace lists rooms and equipment such as Meeting room A, TV Screen, Video conferencing and Power outlets, with capacity details.

references.title: Override availability despite conflicts
references.question: Q4
references.take: SavvyCal's 'Override availability' pop-up shows attendee conflicts and lets you force the time anyway.

references.title: Resource type with quantity for booking
references.question: Q4
references.take: Understory models resources as their own type with a defined quantity. That is how the system could prevent double-booking, though no live conflict warning is shown at creation.

references.title: Session form without conflict feedback
references.question: Q4
references.take: Understory's create or edit session pop-up has a 'Resources: 1 rule' field. It shows no availability or conflict feedback in the form.

references.title: Already in another meeting at join
references.question: Q4
references.take: Zoom alerts 'You are already in another meeting' and offers to start the meeting anyway or handle the conflict.

references.title: Confirm attendance with Attend button
references.question: Q5
references.take: Aboard shows event details with attendance status and an 'Attend' button, then a confirmed attendance view with a checkmark.

references.title: Ticket tiers with capacity limits
references.question: Q5
references.take: Eventbrite's Tickets tab shows capacity such as 0/25 general and 0/20 student, sold status, and an option to edit capacity.

references.title: Guest list with capacity and statuses
references.question: Q5
references.take: Luma shows a guest list with a capacity cap of 1000, pending, invited and attended statuses, and role-based permissions for attendance.

references.title: Mark sessions completed or no-show
references.question: Q5
references.take: Lyssna prompts the host to mark attendance, mark sessions complete or no-show, and automatically marks unmarked sessions after five days.

references.title: RSVP with plus-one from event details
references.question: Q5
references.take: Partiful models sign-up as an RSVP with an explicit plus-one. Capacity is tracked per invitee rather than as a generic ticket count.

references.title: Guest marked as checked in
references.question: Q5
references.take: Posh changes a guest's status to 'Set Checked In', shows confirmation, then lists the guest with a checked-in label.

references.title: Invite another guest after scheduling
references.question: Q5
references.take: SavvyCal lets you add attendees to an already-scheduled event through an 'Invite a guest' pop-up. Attendance stays editable after creation.

references.title: Edit capacity on date and location block
references.question: Q5
references.take: Understory edits capacity as its own step directly on the date and location block, apart from other event fields.

references.title: Reschedule from availability time slots
references.question: Q6
references.take: Cal.com generates time slots from a week and day availability grid tied to the organiser's working hours. Time zone conversion sits behind the slot grid rather than a manual selector.

references.title: Availability page with time zone settings
references.question: Q6
references.take: Cal.com's availability page shows the time zone Asia/Jakarta, weekly hours from 9:00 to 17:00, date overrides and buffer settings.

references.title: Book meeting with zone and duration
references.question: Q6
references.take: Clockwise's booking flow covers a duration preset, a date and time picker with time zone Asia/Jakarta, confirmation and a success message.

references.title: Interview start time plus duration
references.question: Q6
references.take: Homerun uses start time plus a duration dropdown such as 60 min. The time zone is only a read-only label, not a selector.

references.title: Session form with zone and duration
references.question: Q6
references.take: Kajabi's create session pop-up shows a time zone picker for New York, a 30-minute duration, a calendar picker and a time slot selector.

references.title: New event form from empty events list
references.question: Q6
references.take: Microsoft Teams walks from a screen with no events yet through the full new-event form. Start date and time controls arrive with default values already filled in.

references.title: Duration presets with time zone
references.question: Q6
references.take: SavvyCal's availability form has a time zone selector for US/Canada, duration options such as 30 and 15 min, and a time grid.

references.title: Propose meeting across time zones
references.question: Q6
references.take: Upwork proposes a meeting from chat with a date and time picker that supports multiple time zones such as America/New_York, plus duration selection.

references.title: Schedule meeting with zone and duration
references.question: Q6
references.take: Zoom's meeting form shows a time zone selector such as GMT-7:00 Pacific, duration with hour and minute inputs, and recurring meeting controls.
